# Armada

> Every coding agent you have running, on one screen. A macOS menu bar app for someone running
> many Claude Code and Codex sessions at once: what each session is doing, how full its context
> window is, and how much of each plan is left, read locally from what the agents already write
> to disk.

On sale, and not yet downloadable: a licence can be bought at https://armada.mgcrea.io/buy, and the
first release, 1.0.0, is being prepared. macOS 26 or later, and macOS only. The first release will
be a Developer ID signed, notarized zip published on GitHub releases. Not affiliated with Anthropic
or OpenAI.

## What it shows

- Sessions, per account: every live Claude Code session with its title, project, age and state
  (busy, waiting or idle), read from Claude Code's own session registry rather than inferred. A
  waiting session says what it wants. Sorted by what needs you, groupable by project.
- Context: how full each session's context window is, where it started, how fast it has grown,
  and when it was last compacted.
- Plan limits: the 5-hour and 7-day windows per account, with reset times, a pace line and a
  forecast. Claude accounts and Codex homes side by side. Claude limits are asked of the
  account's own `claude` in a request that costs no tokens, falling back to the cache on disk,
  with a badge saying which answered and how old the figure is.
- Accounts: `~/.claude`, every `~/.claude-*` sibling and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; `~/.codex` and
  `CODEX_HOME`.

## What it does

- Starts `claude` or `codex` in a chosen folder on a chosen account, in a terminal. Armada never
  owns the agent process.
- Forks a session from where it stands, through each vendor's own fork command. The original is
  left alone.
- Focus brings forward the application a Claude Code session runs in. Codex sessions have no
  Focus, because Codex records no process id on disk.
- Middle and extra mouse buttons can cycle the session list or send a keystroke.
- The menu bar glyph fills while a session is working and rings when one wants attention.

## Privacy and security

- Armada reaches no network on its own. The one exception is the update check, off until you
  turn it on. It reads one file, armada.mgcrea.io/appcast.xml, which redirects to the GitHub
  release, and sends no identifier: not your licence key, not a machine id.
- The licence key is verified offline, on your Mac, with a signature check. No licence server is
  ever contacted by the app.
- It never writes to Claude Code's or Codex's configuration; `~/.claude*` and `~/.codex` are read
  only. It holds no vendor credentials and never opens Codex's `auth.json`.
- What it writes: its preferences, usage history in
  `~/Library/Application Support/io.mgcrea.armada` (kept 30 days, deletable from Settings), and a
  startup script in its own temporary folder when you start a session.
- `make audit` checks the no-network claim against every build: every Mach-O swept for URL
  loading, DNS and TLS symbols, with one narrowly named exception for Sparkle.
- Not sandboxed, by design: it has to read other tools' folders.
- The `claude` it asks for plan limits talks to Anthropic over your own sign-in. That is the
  program's job, not Armada's.
